possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly. Rain has fallen over areas that saw heavy
rainfall Thursday.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.

Arroyos, streams, and rivers can become raging killer currents in a
matter of minutes, even from distant rainfall.

properties.description:

potential for heavy rainfall during this period. Thunderstorms
embedded in the more general rainfall will have the potential to
produce flash flooding, particularly over recent burn scars.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Custer county.

* WHEN...From 6 PM MDT this evening through Sunday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of creeks,
streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Flooding
may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- 1 to 2.5 inches of rainfall is forecast across the watch area
Friday night through Sunday. Locally heavier accumulations up to
4 inches are possible where thunderstorm activity develops.
- Any recent burn scars from this summer will have elevated Flash
Flood potential.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Please monitor forecasts and be alert for possible Flood Warnings.
Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared to take
action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 18 at 10:20AM MDT by NWS Riverton WY
properties.description:
ESFRIW

A wet weather system will support periods of showers and
thunderstorms across Wyoming Friday, Saturday, and Sunday. This
weather system is funneling abundant tropical moisture into the
state. Given this anomalously high moisture, many thunderstorms will
feature heavy rainfall, possibly leading to localized flooding. Poor
drainage areas, urban areas, and steep terrain will be the most
susceptible locations for this isolated flooding.

Many locations could see rainfall totals anywhere between 0.75" to
1.75" through Sunday afternoon, with a majority of this rain falling
quickly in thunderstorms.

Remember, if you encounter a flooded roadway, turn around don't down!

The St. Louis Clean Air Partnership has issued an air quality alert
for the St. Louis metropolitan area from 10 AM to 8 PM CDT Friday.

An Orange air quality forecast means that maximum ozone
concentrations are expected to reach levels that pose a health risk.
Adverse health effects increase as air quality deteriorates. Ground-
level ozone is an air contaminant which can cause breathing
difficulties for children, older adults, as well as persons with
respiratory problems.

Reducing outdoor physical activity is recommended. If it is a
regularly scheduled work day you are urged to consider
telecommuting, carpooling, or utilizing public transit. Avoid
excessive idling and do not top off when refueling motor vehicles.
The use of gasoline-powered lawn equipment should be reduced or
postponed until late in the day.
